explain.say: Underground, rainwater fills the tiny gaps between grains of sand, gravel and cracked rock. A layer full of water like this is called an aquifer, and its top is the water table.

faq.a: The water table is the top of the zone underground where every gap in the soil and rock is full of water. Below it lies the aquifer that wells draw from.
asks: Where does well water come from?

faq.q: Why is the pump at the bottom of a deep well?
faq.a: Air pressure can only push water up about 10 metres into a suction pump, and less in practice. A pump down in the water pushes it up instead, so it can lift water from hundreds of metres.

faq.q: What is the pressure tank for?
faq.a: It stores pumped water under pressure, using a squeezed pocket of air. Taps can draw from it smoothly, and the pump only starts when the pressure drops low.
asks: Why does a well have a tank?

faq.a: Yes. If water is pumped out faster than rain refills the aquifer, or in a long drought, the water table can sink below the bottom of the well.
Water filtered slowly through rock is often clean, but it can pick up germs or minerals, so well water should be tested regularly.
asks: Is it safe to drink well water?

facts: Suction pumps can lift water only about 7 metres in practice, so deep wells use submersible pumps that push water up.
An aquifer is a layer of rock or sediment whose pores and cracks are filled with groundwater.
